3856.unvetted: CUL Or.1080 6.12 (PGP 19773): seen at 1316x2000 px plus 1424 px crops, four lines of about 45-60 rapid cursive stroke-and-hook signs and about 20 below; the script is not identified (Arabic-script or Hebrew-script shorthand, siyaq, numerals or another hand), no one has transcribed it, so ciphertext is not shown to exist. Needs a palaeographer (Bohak, Elbaum, a siyaq or Arabic shorthand specialist) or the CUL Genizah Unit to say what script it is; PGP: needs examination.

3857.unvetted: T-S Ar.39.472 (PGP 20963): both sides seen at 1626x2000 px with a 2000 px crop; a structured table of about 45 cells, each with a red ordinal, a large abjad heading letter, a numeral column (9, 6, 4, 3, 2, 1 pattern) and rows of non-word Arabic letters; layout is that of a letter-science, divination or calculation table, not a message, but a coded text is not excluded. Needs an Arabic ilm al-huruf or jafr specialist to name the table type; no edition, no key and no decipherment found.

seen.where: CUDL IIIF images.lib.cam.ac.uk MS-OR-01080-00014-00013 (14.13 recto 1505x2000 px, verso 1200x1652 px, native 2568x3412) and MS-OR-01080-00014-00025 (14.25 recto 1542x2000 px, verso 1200x1604 px), viewed 26 Nov 2026
seen.extent: 14.13 recto: seven underlined lines of about 20-30 marks each; verso shows only ink offset. 14.25 recto: strokes-and-numerals line, ring-ended signs and a diagram; verso: a boxed diagram of ring-ended charakteres with a three-line red Arabic caption.
seen.cipher: No cipher shown. 14.13 holds underlined strings of alif-like strokes mixed with Eastern Arabic digits (9, 8, 4) and a few hooked letters, the usual look of an amulet sign series; 14.25 holds ring-ended charakteres in a box and a red Arabic caption (basmala; protects against iron, guns, spears and whatever one fears). No plaintext, key or gloss is written on or with either leaf, and no linguistic content is evident in the marks.

3858.closed: An amulet (red caption on 14.25 verso: protection against iron, guns, spears) whose marks are charakteres and stroke-and-digit sign series with no demonstrated linguistic content, so no ciphertext is shown; kept closed unless a magic-text specialist shows an encoded text. The 25 Nov sweep's 'letter-number code' was a guess from the stroke-and-digit lines.
